assumptions: 'Success rate' means attempt-level success rate: successful attempts divided by all attempts, with each retry counted as a separate attempt. Order-level and technical rates are shown alongside.
Period: 2026-10-18..2026-10-31 compared with 2026-10-04..2026-10-17 (the immediately preceding period of equal length).
caveats: Duplicate records on 12 Oct: 341 attempts were ingested twice (11,704 raw rows vs 11,363 unique attempts, +3.0%). Paysight counts each attempt once. Handling: removed in the clean view (first ingestion kept).

Volume spike 18 Oct–31 Oct: Attempt volume was +39% versus the usual level for those weekdays over 14 day(s). Real business events (sales) and data gaps both look like this; check before comparing totals across this period. Handling: not a data error by itself; flagged for context.
Success rate depends on the denominator: attempt-level 88.54%, order-level 90.89%, technical 92.11% (retries and drop-offs explain the gap).

facts.text: Attempt success rate fell 1.47pp from 90.0% (148,791 successes out of 165,297 attempts) to 88.5% (203,741 successes out of 230,100 attempts).
By payment method, mix shift contributed -1.00pp of the drop, primarily driven by CARD_EMI increasing its share of attempts from 2.9% to 10.9% while holding a lower success rate of 81.6%.
NovaMart expanded its share of total attempts from 6.0% to 30.0%, while its success rate fell from 90.0% to 86.2%, accounting for -0.96pp of the overall -1.47pp change.
Like-for-like performance drops across payment methods accounted for -0.47pp, led by DEBIT_CARD where success rates fell 2.65pp from 86.0% to 83.4%.
Within debit cards, Harbor Bank experienced a 9.44pp drop from 86.2% to 76.7%, contributing -0.39pp to the overall decline.
For Harbor Bank debit cards, ISSUER_RISK_DECLINE increased by 10.8 failures per 100 attempts, rising from 0.32 to 11.12 failures per 100 attempts.
Overall attempt-level success rate was 88.5%, order-level success rate was 90.9%, and technical success rate was 92.1% in the recent two-week window.

response.headline: Payment attempt success rate fell 1.47pp from 90.0% to 88.5%. The drop was driven by traffic shifting toward lower-converting payment methods like CARD_EMI alongside a surge in NovaMart volume, combined with like-for-like rate drops concentrated in Harbor Bank debit card transactions.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Engage Harbor Bank's issuer operations or risk team to confirm rule changes or threshold adjustments deployed between 18 Oct and 31 Oct.
hypotheses.rationale: Harbor Bank debit card failures were overwhelmingly driven by ISSUER_RISK_DECLINE, which jumped from 0.32 to 11.12 per 100 attempts, while other error categories remained relatively stable.
hypotheses.text: Harbor Bank updated or tightened its debit card fraud risk rules during the period.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Confirm with the NovaMart account management team whether a major sales event or marketing push ran between 18 Oct and 31 Oct.
hypotheses.rationale: Overall volume spiked 39%, NovaMart traffic share expanded from 6.0% to 30.0%, and EMI share increased from 2.9% to 10.9% alongside a rise in EMI_NOT_ELIGIBLE declines.
hypotheses.text: A promotional shopping campaign at NovaMart increased higher-friction payment attempts like EMI and cards.

recommendations.rationale: Harbor Bank debit card transactions saw ISSUER_RISK_DECLINE rise by 10.8 per 100 attempts, driving significant like-for-like degradation.
